question: A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician because of hearing loss and unsteadiness while standing and walking for the past 2 months. She needs support from a wall to prevent herself from falling. She has not had any recent injuries and has no history of serious illness. Vital signs are within normal limits. Examination shows an unsteady gait. She sways when asked to stand upright with her feet together. She is unable to hear fingers rubbing next to her ears or repeat words whispered in her ears bilaterally. An MRI of the brain shows a 3-cm tumor in the right cerebellopontine angle and a 4.5-cm tumor in the left cerebellopontine angle. This patient is most likely to develop which of the following in the future?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "22-year-old woman with hearing loss and unsteadiness" -> "MRI shows tumors in cerebellopontine angle" -> "suggestive of vestibular schwannomas" -> "associated with Neurofibromatosis Type II" -> "increased risk of meningiomas" -> 85%

CHAIN: "22-year-old woman with bilateral tumors in cerebellopontine angle" -> "indicates possible genetic syndrome" -> "Neurofibromatosis Type II" -> "characterized by multiple tumors" -> "including meningiomas" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with unsteady gait and hearing loss" -> "MRI reveals bilateral tumors" -> "consistent with vestibular schwannomas" -> "often seen in Neurofibromatosis Type II" -> "which predisposes to meningiomas" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Bilateral cerebellopontine angle tumors found" -> "likely vestibular schwannomas" -> "associated with Neurofibromatosis Type II" -> "increased risk of developing meningiomas" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with bilateral tumors in the cerebellopontine angle, which is suggestive of bilateral vestibular schwannomas, commonly associated with Neurofibromatosis type II (NF2). NF2 is characterized by the development of bilateral vestibular schwannomas and other tumors, including meningiomas and ependymomas. Among the options provided, meningioma is the most likely future development due to its association with NF2.
